summary: Source review at6aee8ee maps the requested OpenTelemetry resiliency benchmark to existing UTEL receipt transport without selecting an exporter migration or new acceptance gate. The client has five attempts with per-attempt cancellation; immutable producer queues preserve pending intent, exact identity and bytes on capacity/uncertainty. Maintained tests cover receiver process exits at durability/application cuts, producer intent/enqueue/cursor hook cuts, TLS lost-response and same-identity recovery, deduplication/conflict/expiry, configuration refusal and correction ordering/projection. These are inspected executable assertions, not a fresh passing run or installed fault qualification. Producer hook exceptions do not prove an actual killed producer; separate retry/spool controls do not establish the integrated complete-budget outage scenario. Direct storage-operation ENOSPC/EIO, failing flush/fsync or SQLite FULL/IOERR was not found in the five inspected telemetry test files; adjacent injected exceptions establish their control-flow scope only. A deterministic actual SQLite commit-failure fixture is a possible narrow future selection, not a new completion prerequisite or physical failed-media proof. Persisted intent, local immutable retention, remote durable receipt and applied/corrected facts remain distinct; retry never authorizes replay of an uncertain workload. Accepted4705 normal durable receipt and4707 receiver/browser scope remain reusable with original source/configuration limits; they do not qualify every fault, complete attribution, recovery/correction, retention/rollback or assessment/adoption. Root retains current custody and remaining operation selection; historical batch2 pending, deleted client credentials, original failures/Unknown effects and439+46holds are not changed by this source review.
title: UTEL source fault controls and installed acceptance remain separate
